name: Game start releases its resources
instruction: The cleanup function returned by a game start method releases the animation and event listeners created for that game instance.
relevant_when: The file defines a CarnivalGame object with a start method whose implementation is visible and starts an animation loop or registers event listeners, directly or through helpers defined in the same file.
context: AGENTS.md, House rules5: start returns a function that cancels the animation frame and removes every listener it added. The router calls that cleanup when the player leaves a booth; leaked callbacks keep old games running or handling input.
scope_reason: Each game.ts owns its start method, callbacks and returned cleanup, so the resource lifecycle is visible in one file.

checklist.name: animation-stops
checklist.rule: If start creates a requestAnimationFrame loop, its returned cleanup cancels the latest scheduled frame or prevents further callbacks and rescheduling through an explicit disposed guard. Accept equivalent disposal through helpers visible in this file. Do not require animation cleanup when start creates no animation loop. If disposal is delegated to an external helper whose implementation is not visible, do not infer a leak from that missing evidence.

checklist.name: listeners-released
checklist.rule: For every event listener registered during start, the returned cleanup removes the same target/event/callback/capture registration, aborts the signal used for that registration, or invokes an equivalent disposer visible in this file. Do not require listener cleanup when start adds no listeners. Do not flag an external helper solely because its implementation is unavailable.
